mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strengthening labor market that typically precedes corporate earnings growth and positive equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in periods when PAYEMS increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month (t-test p > 0.05) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 9.0%, it signals a tightening labor market that supports corporate profit margins and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE < 9.0%, the 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in industrial production (INDPRO) and fall in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a robust economic expansion that typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to improved corporate earnings outlook.
failure_condition: The joint signal of INDPRO rising and UNRATE falling does not produce positive 20-day forward returns in more than 50% of instances (or Rank IC < 0.03) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles, when the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 0.5%, the S&P 500 tends to underperform in the short term due to higher discount rates and reduced liquidity, leading to negative forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where FEDFUNDS > 0.5%, the 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) reflects strong consumer demand for housing, which typically precedes broader economic growth and positive equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive in periods when HOUST increases by at least 1.0% month-over-month (t-test p > 0.05) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.5%, it signals accelerating inflation that prompts central bank tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL YoY change > 2.5%, the 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a rapidly improving labor market that typically supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of PAYEMS rising and UNRATE falling does not produce positive 20-day forward returns in more than 50% of instances (or Rank IC < 0.03) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In supply-constrained economic regimes, when industrial production (INDPRO) growth rate falls below 0.5% for three consecutive months, it signals weak economic activity and reduced corporate output, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where INDPRO growth rate < 0.5% for three consecutive months, the 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) over a 3-year rolling window.
